cues.en: Nothing in the universe is static.
cues.zh: 宇宙中没有任何事物是静止的。

cues.en: In the Milky Way, billions of stars orbit the galactic center. Some, like our sun, are pretty consistent,
cues.zh: 在银河系中，数十亿颗恒星围绕银心运行。有些恒星，比如我们的太阳，相当稳定，

cues.en: keeping a distance of around 30,000
cues.zh: 与银心保持着大约三万

cues.en: light years from the galactic center, completing an orbit every two hundred and thirty million years.
cues.zh: 光年的距离，每两亿三千万年完成一圈公转。

cues.en: This dance is not an orderly ballet, more like a skating rink filled with drunk toddlers.
cues.zh: 这场舞蹈并非井然有序的芭蕾，更像是一个挤满了醉酒幼儿的溜冰场。

cues.en: This chaos makes the galaxy dangerous.
cues.zh: 这种混乱让银河系变得危险。

cues.en: Our solar neighborhood is constantly changing with stars moving hundreds of kilometers every second.
cues.zh: 我们所在的太阳邻域一直在变化，恒星每秒移动数百公里。

cues.en: Only the vast distances between objects protect us from the dangers out there.
cues.zh: 只有天体之间巨大的距离才让我们免受外部危险的侵袭。

cues.en: But we might get unlucky in the future.
cues.zh: 但未来我们可能会不走运。

cues.en: At some point, we can encounter a star going supernova
cues.zh: 在某个时刻，我们可能遇到一颗即将超新星爆发的恒星，

cues.en: or a massive object passing by and showering Earth with asteroids.
cues.zh: 或是一个巨大天体经过，向地球倾泻小行星。

cues.en: If something like this were to happen, we would likely know thousands,
cues.zh: 如果发生这样的情况，我们很可能提前数千、

cues.en: if not millions of years in advance.
cues.zh: 甚至数百万年就会知道。

cues.en: But we still couldn't do much about it
cues.zh: 但我们仍然无能为力，

cues.en: unless
cues.zh: 除非

cues.en: we move our whole solar system out of the way.
cues.zh: 我们把整个太阳系移开。

cues.en: To move the solar system, we need a stellar engine,
cues.zh: 要移动太阳系，我们需要一台恒星引擎，

cues.en: a megastructure
cues.zh: 一种巨型结构，

cues.en: used to steer a star through the galaxy.
cues.zh: 用来在银河系中驾驶恒星。

cues.en: It's the kind of thing that might be built by an advanced civilization
cues.zh: 这种东西可能由先进文明建造，

cues.en: with Dyson sphere level technology
cues.zh: 拥有戴森球级别的技术，

cues.en: that's thinking about their future millions of years ahead of time.
cues.zh: 并且提前数百万年考虑自己的未来。

cues.en: But how do we possibly move the hundreds of thousands of objects in the solar system?
cues.zh: 但我们怎么可能移动太阳系中数十万个天体呢？

cues.en: The good news is we can ignore all of that. We only need to move the sun, all the other stuff is glued to it by gravity, gravity and will follow it wherever it decides to go.
cues.zh: 好消息是，我们可以完全忽略那些。我们只需要移动太阳，其他所有东西都被引力束缚着，会跟随太阳去任何它去的地方。

cues.en: There are lots of ideas about what a stellar engine might look like and how it would work.
cues.zh: 关于恒星引擎长什么样、如何运作，有很多设想。

cues.en: We've picked two grounded in our current understanding of physics that could be built in theory.
cues.zh: 我们挑选了两种基于当前物理学认知、理论上可以建造的方案。

cues.en: The simplest kind of stellar engine is the Shkadov thruster,
cues.zh: 最简单的恒星引擎是什卡多夫推进器，

cues.en: a giant mirror.
cues.zh: 一面巨大的镜子。

cues.en: It works on the same principle as a rocket.
cues.zh: 它的工作原理和火箭相同。

cues.en: Like rocket fuel, the photons released as solar radiation carry momentum.
cues.zh: 就像火箭燃料一样，太阳辐射释放的光子携带动量。

cues.en: Not a lot, but a bit. For example, if an astronaut turned on a flashlight in space, it would push them backwards very, very slowly.
cues.zh: 动量不大，但确实有一点。比如，如果宇航员在太空中打开手电筒，手电筒会以极慢的速度把他向后推。

cues.en: A stellar engine will work a little better than a flashlight because the sun produces a lot of photons.
cues.zh: 恒星引擎的效果会比手电筒好一些，因为太阳产生的光子非常多。

cues.en: The basic idea of the shutoff thruster is to reflect up to half of the solar radiation to create thrust and slowly push the sun where we want it to go.
cues.zh: 什卡多夫推进器的基本思路是反射最多一半的太阳辐射来产生推力，慢慢把太阳推向我们想要它去的方向。

cues.en: In order for the shutoff thruster to work, it must be kept in the same place, not orbiting the sun.
cues.zh: 要让什卡多夫推进器正常工作，它必须保持在固定位置，而不是绕太阳轨道运行。

cues.en: Although the sun's gravity will try to put it in, it would be supported by radiation pressure, which props the mirror up.
cues.zh: 虽然太阳引力会试图把它拉进去，但辐射压会支撑它，把镜子托住。

cues.en: This means the mirror would have to be very light, made of micron thin reflecting foil from materials like aluminium alloys.
cues.zh: 这意味着镜子必须非常轻，由微米级厚度的反射箔制成，材料如铝合金。

cues.en: The mirror's shape is important too.
cues.zh: 镜子的形状也很重要。

cues.en: Enveloping the sun in a giant spherical shell wouldn't work because that would refocus light back to the sun, heating it up and creating all sorts of unpleasant problems.
cues.zh: 用巨大的球壳包裹太阳行不通，因为那会把光线重新聚焦回太阳，使其升温，制造出各种麻烦问题。

cues.en: Instead,
cues.zh: 相反，

cues.en: we use a parabola,
cues.zh: 我们用一个抛物面，

cues.en: which sends most of the photons around the sun and in the same direction,
cues.zh: 它把大部分光子引向太阳周围并朝向同一个方向，

cues.en: which maximizes thrust.
cues.zh: 从而最大化推力。

cues.en: To prevent accidentally
cues.zh: 为了防止因阳光过多或过少而意外地

cues.en: burning or freezing earth with too much or too little sunlight, the only safe place to build a is
cues.zh: 烧焦或冻结地球，建造它的唯一安全位置是

cues.en: over the sun's poles.
cues.zh: 在太阳的两极上方。

cues.en: This means we can only move the sun vertically in the plane of the solar system and one direction in the Milky Way, which limits our travel options a bit.
cues.zh: 这意味着我们只能在太阳系平面内垂直移动太阳，在银河系中只能朝一个方向移动，这在一定程度上限制了我们的旅行选择。

cues.en: But that is basically it.
cues.zh: 但基本上就是这样。

cues.en: For a civilization capable of building a Dyson sphere, this is a relatively simple endeavor.
cues.zh: 对于一个能够建造戴森球的文明来说，这是一个相对简单的尝试。

cues.en: Not complicated,
cues.zh: 并不复杂，

cues.en: just very hard to build.
cues.zh: 只是建造难度极高。

cues.en: At full throttle, the solar system could probably be moved by about a 100 light years over two hundred and thirty million years.
cues.zh: 在全速运转下，太阳系在大约两亿三千万年内大概可以移动100光年左右。

cues.en: Over a few billion years, it gives us near complete control over the sun's orbit in the galaxy.
cues.zh: 在几十亿年的时间里，它能让我们几乎完全掌控太阳在银河系中的轨道。

cues.en: But in the short term, this might not be fast enough to dodge a deadly supernova.
cues.zh: 但在短期内，这可能还不够快，无法躲避致命的超新星爆发。

cues.en: That's why we thought we could do better.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么我们认为我们可以做得更好。

cues.en: So we asked our astrophysicist
cues.zh: 所以我们请我们的天体物理学家

cues.en: friend if he could design a faster stellar engine for this video.
cues.zh: 朋友为这期视频设计一个更快的恒星发动机。

cues.en: He did and wrote a paper about it that's been published in a peer reviewed journal.
cues.zh: 他照办了，并写了一篇关于它的论文，发表在同行评议的期刊上。

cues.en: You can find it in our sources document.
cues.zh: 你可以在我们的参考资料文档中找到它。

cues.en: We're
cues.zh: 我们将

cues.en: going to call our new stellar engine the Kaplan thruster.
cues.zh: 把这个新的恒星发动机称为卡普兰推进器。

cues.en: It works a lot like a traditional rocket.
cues.zh: 它的工作原理很像传统火箭。

cues.en: Shoot exhaust one way to push yourself the other.
cues.zh: 向一个方向喷射尾气来把你自己推向另一个方向。

cues.en: It's a large space station platform powered by a Dyson sphere that gathers matter from the sun to power nuclear fusion.
cues.zh: 它是一个大型空间站平台，由戴森球提供动力，收集太阳物质来为核聚变提供能量。

cues.en: It shoots out a very fast jet of particles at nearly 1% the speed of light out of the solar system.
cues.zh: 它以接近光速 1% 的极高速度向太阳系外喷射出一道极快的粒子流。

cues.en: A second jet pushes the sun along like a tugboat.
cues.zh: 第二道喷流像拖船一样推动着太阳前进。

cues.en: The Kaplan thruster requires a lot of fuel, millions of tons per second.
cues.zh: 卡普兰推进器需要消耗大量燃料，每秒数百万吨。

cues.en: To gather this fuel, our thruster uses very large electromagnetic
cues.zh: 为了收集这些燃料，我们的推进器使用极大的电磁

cues.en: fields to funnel hydrogen and helium from the solar wind into the engine.
cues.zh: 场将太阳风中的氢和氦汇集到发动机中。

cues.en: The solar wind alone doesn't provide enough fuel though, and that's where the comes
cues.zh: 仅靠太阳风还不足以提供足够的燃料，而这正是

cues.en: in.
cues.zh: 发挥作用的地方。

cues.en: Using its power, sunlight can be refocused to the surface of the sun.
cues.zh: 利用其能量，阳光可以被重新聚焦到太阳表面。

cues.en: This heats small regions to extreme temperatures, lifting billions of tons of mass off the sun.
cues.zh: 这会使小片区域加热到极端温度，从而从太阳表面剥离数十亿吨的物质。

cues.en: This mass can be collected and separated into hydrogen and helium.
cues.zh: 这些物质可以被收集并分离成氢和氦。

cues.en: The helium is burned explosively in thermonuclear fusion reactors.
cues.zh: 氦气会在热核聚变反应堆中发生爆炸性燃烧。

cues.en: A jet of radioactive oxygen at a temperature of nearly a billion degrees is expelled and becomes our primary source of propulsion from our stellar engine.
cues.zh: 温度接近十亿度的放射性氧气喷流被喷射出来，成为我们这台恒星发动机的主要推进力来源。

cues.en: To prevent the engine from just crashing into the sun, it needs to balance itself.
cues.zh: 为了防止发动机直接撞向太阳，它需要保持自身平衡。

cues.en: To do this, we accelerate the collected hydrogen with electromagnetic
cues.zh: 为此，我们使用粒子加速器产生的电磁

cues.en: fields using particle accelerators and shoot a jet back at the sun.
cues.zh: 场加速收集到的氢气，并向太阳喷射出一道喷流。

cues.en: This balances the thruster and transfers the thrust of our engine back to the sun.
cues.zh: 这平衡了推进器，并将我们发动机的推力传递回太阳。

cues.en: In as little as a million years, this engine can move the sun by 50 light years, more than enough to dodge a supernova.
cues.zh: 只需短短一百万年，这台发动机就能把太阳移动 50 光年，这足以躲避超新星爆发。

cues.en: At full throttle, the solar system can be completely redirected in its galactic orbit in ten million years.
cues.zh: 全速运转下，太阳系可以在一千万年内彻底改变它在银河系中的运行轨道。

cues.en: But wait, won't we use up the sun this way?
cues.zh: 等等，这样不会把太阳用光吗？

cues.en: Fortunately,
cues.zh: 幸运的是，

cues.en: the sun is so massive that even billions of tons of material will barely scratch the surface.
cues.zh: 太阳的质量极大，就算抽取数十亿吨物质，也几乎只是刮到它的表面。

cues.en: In fact, this megastructure will actually extend our sun's life since lower stars burn slower,
cues.zh: 事实上，这种巨型结构反而会延长太阳的寿命，因为较小的恒星燃烧得更慢，

cues.en: keeping the solar system inhabitable for many more billions of years.
cues.zh: 让太阳系在未来数十亿年里都能继续适宜居住。

cues.en: With a Kaplan thruster, we could turn the entire solar system into our spaceship.
cues.zh: 有了 Kaplan 推进器，我们就能把整个太阳系变成我们的宇宙飞船。

cues.en: For example, by orbiting backwards in the galaxy and colonizing hundreds or thousands of stars as we pass by them.
cues.zh: 比如让它在银河系中反向运行，并在经过数百或数千颗恒星时将它们殖民。

cues.en: It may even be possible to escape the galaxy entirely and expand beyond the Milky Way.
cues.zh: 我们甚至可能彻底逃离银河系，向银河系之外扩张。

cues.en: Stellar engines are the kind of machines built by civilizations thinking not in terms of years or decades,
cues.zh: 恒星发动机是由那些不以年或十年为时间尺度思考的文明制造的机器，

cues.en: but eons.
cues.zh: 而是以万古为尺度。

cues.en: Since we know that our sun will die one day, a stellar engine could allow the far future descendants of humans to travel to other stars without ever having to venture into the terrifying dark abyss of interstellar space.
cues.zh: 既然我们知道太阳终有一天会死亡，恒星发动机就能让人类遥远未来的后代前往其他恒星，而不必踏入那片可怕的星际黑暗深渊。

cues.en: Until we build a stellar engine, we're adrift and subject to the whims of the Galactic Sea.
cues.zh: 在我们建造恒星发动机之前，我们只能随波漂流，任由银河之海摆布。

cues.en: We may not like where it leads us.
cues.zh: 我们未必会喜欢它把我们带到的地方。

cues.en: Maybe our descendants will set sail and become an interstellar species
cues.zh: 也许我们的后代会扬帆起航，成为一个星际物种，

cues.en: for millions of years to come.
cues.zh: 延续数百万年。

cues.en: This was our last video for the year 12019
cues.zh: 这是我们在人类纪元 12019 年发布的最后一期视频，

cues.en: of the human era, and what a year it was.
cues.zh: 而这一年真是非同寻常。

cues.en: So much stuff happened everywhere
cues.zh: 发生了那么多事

cues.en: to so many different people.
cues.zh: 涉及那么多不同的人。

cues.en: Calendars and holidays are just imaginary,
cues.zh: 日历和节日只是虚构的，

cues.en: but they help us to cut our lives into pieces that our brains can handle.
cues.zh: 但它们帮我们把生活切成大脑能够处理的碎片。

cues.en: We're leaving 12019
cues.zh: 我们将12019年

cues.en: behind with a weird mixture of disillusion and hope.
cues.zh: 抛在身后，带着幻灭与希望交织的复杂心情。

cues.en: The world is screwed up, but we can fix it. In a few days, this year will be over, and we'll get to try again.
cues.zh: 世界虽然一团糟，但我们能修复它。几天后，这一年就要结束了，我们将迎来崭新的一试。

cues.en: Thank you for watching our videos and for sticking around for so many years.
cues.zh: 感谢大家观看我们的视频，并陪伴了这么多年。

cues.en: See you all in 12020.
